budget_items.topic: Cowry Nature Center ADA trail/parking grant
budget_items.what_was_said: The consultant said remaining grant funds were confirmed available to study an alternate trail alignment that could avoid direct wetland alteration, after a delay getting an answer from the town. An extra-services agreement was prepared to cover the additional design study.

Mike proposed buying a hardwired smoke/CO2 detector for the basement and a hardwired smoke detector plus one battery unit for the hallway, per the fire department's recommendation, to be purchased at Home Depot and installed by him.

A third flooring quote was being obtained from Wayne Amo Flooring, which can offer prevailing wages; carpet was described as the least expensive option and more forgiving than vinyl plank, which came in significantly more expensive.
Mike listed the removed wood stove for sale on Facebook Marketplace and noted the fire bricks are in rough shape and should be replaced before a new owner uses it.
The chair said the department is still in limbo closing out the previous budget and there were no new budget updates to discuss.

The storm water committee is drafting a warrant article to propose establishing a storm water utility, not yet establishing it, because the operational budget cannot fund DPW's MS4 permit obligations such as catch basin and culvert cleaning.

decisions.decision: Pollinator habitat will be mowed one more time by the town before conditions wind down for the season.
Commission left the existing 10-business-day document submittal rule in the wetlands regulation unchanged for now, though members noted it could be reconsidered given electronic document access.

Central Mass Mosquito Control, coordinated with the DPW director, will perform drainage/ditch work at 467 Lancaster Ave to alleviate water flow onto the property, as a courtesy notice to the commission.
The commission's agent expressed interest in becoming a licensed pesticide applicator sponsored by the commission; general support was voiced but no formal vote was taken.
Members expressed informal interest in attending an upcoming town forest conference and a Conservation Commission conference in October; no vote taken.

public_comment.stated_role: resident of 50 Sunset Lane on Lake Shirley, former commission member
public_comment.topic: Raised three process concerns: late submittal of revised documents before continued hearings, the timing of public comment relative to commission discussion during hearings, and inconsistent/undocumented justification when the commission grants waivers from regulations.

minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission heard an extended public comment from a former commissioner about hearing-process fairness, then worked through four continued wetlands hearings, voting to pursue a redesigned, wetland-avoiding ADA trail route at Cowry Nature Center and continuing three other hearings to September 16 due to late-submitted documents. The commission also voted to approve draft bylaw amendments to send toward town meeting, approved a $150 purchase for smoke/CO2 detectors at its Hollis Road property, and heard committee updates on storm water utility planning and mosquito-control drainage assistance.

what_happened.line: The Commission voted 5-0 to accept a redesigned ADA trail route at Cowry Nature Center that avoids direct wetland alteration.
Three other wetlands hearings -- a boat ramp, a driveway crossing, and an irrigation pond -- were continued to September 16 after documents arrived late.
The Commission voted 5-0 to approve draft bylaw amendments to move toward town meeting.
A storm water committee is drafting a warrant article for a storm water utility because the operating budget cannot fund the DPW's required catch-basin and culvert cleaning.
The Commission approved an amount as heard purchase for smoke and CO2 detectors at its Hollis Road property.

why_it_matters: The ADA trail redesign changes how a town-funded accessibility project reaches Cowry Nature Center and keeps it clear of wetland permitting delays.
The bylaw amendments the Commission approved will come before town meeting, where residents get a vote.
A storm water utility warrant article, if it advances, could mean a new fee tied to the town's stormwater permit obligations.
